messages.content: write a story where a child starts drawing the garden outside, then rain makes her choose a new part to draw. do not make it a sad story.

a child sits by a window with paper on her desk. she starts with the tree in the garden and wants to add the table next. then rain comes, and she sees how the window changes what she can see. she draws the lines of water on the glass as well as the tree behind it. her mother asks whether the rain stopped her drawing. she says no. it gave her another part of the picture to think about. when she finishes, she has both the garden and the window on the page.
ask my request with starts.
write a story where a child starts drawing the garden, then rain makes her choose another part to draw. keep it happy.
did she take the tree out of the picture?
no. the story keeps the tree behind the glass and puts the window in as another part. she changed the picture without giving up everything she had started.
say that simply.
no. she kept the tree in the picture and drew the window too.
can you give the story a name without the word rain?
the garden through the glass.
help me write a message asking my brother to bring a cup and my sister to bring a plate. do not make it sound like both should bring both things.
for my brother: please bring a cup. for my sister: please bring a plate.
can you make it sound like one message to both of them, using brother and sister?
you could write: could my brother bring a cup and my sister bring a plate, please?
now say i will bring both things instead. keep it short.
i will bring the cup and the plate.
what did that change?
you are now the person bringing both things. the first message gave one request to your brother and another to your sister.
explain simply.
the first message asked two people for one thing each. the new message says you will bring both.
does the new message say the cup and plate are mine?
no. you can bring something that is yours or something that another person has.
say it simply.
no. bringing a thing does not tell us whose it is.
my neighbor asked for a quiet hour while studying. does that mean everyone has to leave the house?
not from that request alone. quiet is about sound. people can stay in the house and do quiet things without leaving.
what can i ask to understand the request better?
you could ask: what would help most during that hour? would no music and everyone talking quietly be enough?
use talking quietly in a short question.
would no music and everyone talking quietly be enough for that hour?
they say that would help. write my reply if i can do that.
okay. i will leave the music off and talk quietly during that hour.
does saying yes for one hour mean i can never play music again?
no. the plan is for one hour while they study. it does not choose what happens every other day.
say my last question simply.
does saying yes for one hour mean i can never play music again?
can you make a short note about how long the quiet time is?
quiet hour for studying. leave music off until the hour is over.
what did i ask for?
you asked for a note making it clear that the quiet plan is for one hour.
i made coffee for my friend, but i do not know if they like it. can you tell from the fact that they drank it?
not for sure. drinking it does not always mean they like it. they may have different reasons for finishing a drink. you can ask how it was without choosing their answer.
use like in a simple answer.
drinking it does not always mean they like it. ask how it was if you want to know.
write a simple question i could ask.
was the coffee how you like it?
they say it was a little different from what they usually drink. does that mean they did not like it?
different does not always mean they did not like it. ask what was different or whether they enjoyed it.
answer simply.
different does not always mean they did not like it. ask what was different or whether they enjoyed it.
write a question that does not ask them to say it was good.
what was different about it?
can i just thank them for telling me if they say they wanted more milk?
yes. you could say: thank you for telling me. i will remember that you like more milk.
my map is only about the park and the street around it. if i cannot see the station on it, does that mean the town has no station?
no. your map is about the park area. the station could be in another part of town that is not on the page.
say it simply.
no. the station could be in another part of town, outside the area on your map.
write a short question for someone at the park.
is there a station near here, and how can i get to it?
what if they say it is too far to be on this small map?
then the map does not have that part of town on it. the station can still be there.
make that simple.
the map does not have that part of town on it. the station can still be there.
can you write that as a short explanation with no real town information?
a small map can show one area. it does not have to show every place in the town.
use show in a short answer.
a small map can show one area. it does not have to show every place in the town.
give me an example where what did she do and why did she do it need different answers.
what did she do? she opened the window. why did she do it? she wanted to hear the music outside. the first answer says what happened, and the other gives the reason.
explain simply.
the first answer says what happened. the other says the reason for it.
can the same person open a window for a different reason?
yes. another person might open it to look at someone near the door or to let air into the room. what they do can look the same while the reason is different.
use what they do in a short answer.
what they do can look the same while the reason is different.
write a short story where someone asks why instead of choosing the reason without knowing.

a boy sees his sister open the window and asks why. she says that she wants to hear their aunt calling from the garden. he had thought she wanted to look at the sky, but he asked rather than saying he knew.
ask my last request simply.
write a story where someone asks for the reason instead of choosing it without knowing.
my brother finished his work before me, and i felt slow. we were not doing the same task, though.
you had different work. one task taking longer does not tell us that the person doing it was wrong or not trying.
say it simply.
different work can take more or less time. the time alone does not tell us how well each person did.
he was putting books away, and i was writing a letter.
those are different things to do. putting books away and choosing words for a letter do not have to finish at the same time.
say that with things to do.
those are different things to do. you do not have to finish them at the same time.
can i take time with my letter even after he is done?
yes. his work is done, but your letter still needs your time.
make it simple.
yes. you can take time to finish your letter.
write a short note for me.
my task can take the time it needs.
make the note shorter.
take time for your task.
in this made up story, one animal has a white face and black legs. can i write that all animals look like that?
no. those details are about the animal in this story. animal is a general word for many different living things, not a rule that they all have the same face or legs.
write two sentences that keep the details specific.
the animal in the story has a white face and black legs. that is how this animal looks, rather than how every animal looks.
ask my last request simply.
write two sentences that keep the details about this animal only.
can another animal in the same story have brown legs?
yes. the word animal does not make the color the same for each one. you can give different details for another animal.
what if i call them both animals and leave out the color of each one?
then people know there are animals, but they do not get the color of each one from that sentence alone.
say it simply.
the general word keeps the kind of thing, but not the color of each one.
can you ask me for the other animal detail?
what does the other animal look like?
i asked my friend when and where to meet. they answered tomorrow morning. did they answer both parts?
no. they gave a general time, but not a place. you still need the where part.
write a reply that only asks what is left.
where should we meet tomorrow morning?
what if they say at the place we always meet, but i am not sure which place they mean?
then ask for the place rather than saying you know. the same words may bring different places to mind for each of you.
give a simple question.
which place do you mean?
they say the library. does that tell me the specific hour?
no. tomorrow morning is still general. the library gives the place, but the hour is another detail to choose.
ask that question simply.
does the library tell me which hour to meet?
ask them for an hour without changing the place.
what time should we meet at the library tomorrow morning?
write a story where someone closes a container and a child thinks the object inside is gone.

a man puts a key in a container and closes it. a child asks where the key went. he says that it is still inside, even though she cannot see it now. she asks him to open it again. the key is there. then she closes it herself and says that the key is still inside unless someone takes it out. he asks how she knows, and she says she saw what happened before the container was closed.
does the story tell us that every closed container has a key?
no. this container has a key because the story said one was put there. closed by itself does not tell us what is inside.
say my last question simply.
does every closed container have a key because this one does?
why is unless someone takes it out useful?
it leaves room for a later change. the key is still there from what they saw, but a person moving it would give new information.
can you add one sentence where the child takes it out herself?
she opens the container, takes out the key, and puts it on the table.
where is the key now?
on the table, from the last change you gave.
good morning, picoboi. i have a little time before school and wanted to say hello.
good morning. it is nice to have a little time to talk. what would you like to do today?
ask what i want to do today.
what would you like to do today?
i want to show my teacher a picture i drew. i do not know if it is good enough.
you can show it as something you made and ask about one part you want to learn more about. you do not need to know everything before asking a question.
say that simply.
you can show what you made and ask a question. that can be part of learning, rather than only something you do after learning everything.
give me a question for the teacher.
could you look at my picture and tell me one thing i could make better?
can i also tell them which part i like?
yes. you could say: i like the tree, but i am not sure about the house. could you help me with that part?
picoboi, write a made up story about me going to a shop. i did not really go there today.

in the story, you walk to a small shop and see a book in the window. you ask a worker if you can look at it. inside is a picture of a place you would like to visit. you read a few pages, then put it back and choose to think before buying it.
use choose in the last sentence.
you read a few pages, then put it back and choose to think before buying it.
if i ask what i bought today, should you use that story?
no. you said the shop visit was made up. the story does not give me a real fact about what you bought today.
what if i say i really bought bread today?
then i can use bread as the real detail you gave. it does not make the made up book story real too.
ask my last question simply.
what if i say i really bought bread today?
now answer the question what did i buy today.
you told me that you bought bread today. the book was only part of the made up story.
